title: Workflows
intro: Build a workflow when you need OpenLDR to receive, check, transform, store or deliver data. A node is one step. Lines connect the output of one node to the input of another.
Use your own records and reporting queries. No documentation sample data is required. The pictures use a separate test installation. Optional fictional practice files are at the end.
View workflows opens definitions and runs. Edit workflows creates and changes them. Run workflows starts manual runs. Manage workflow secrets changes webhook credentials.
The shipped Ingest workflow also handles Forms submissions. Keep it enabled. Editing it affects every sender using its webhook. Replace a secret only when you are ready to update those senders.

tasks.title: Find a workflow
intro: Use this to open an existing definition before inspecting or changing it.
steps: Use Search workflows to filter names. Clear the search to restore the list.
Select the workflow name. This example opens the shipped Ingest workflow.
Select Fit View at the bottom left. Use the plus and minus controls to zoom. Pan moves the canvas; Select draws a selection box.

tasks.title: Set the Ingest webhook secret
intro: Use this when an authorised sender needs a credential you can copy. A saved secret cannot be revealed. Coordinate rotation with the senders first.
steps: Select the gear labelled Configure above the selected node.
Under Secret, select Replace secret. An unsaved value instead offers Regenerate.
Copy the new secret and keep it with your sender credentials. The URL and Header fields show where and how to send it.
Check the system-workflow warning, then select Save anyway when you intend the change.
tasks.result: The Workflow saved message confirms the write. Senders must use the newly saved secret.

tasks.title: Read a run and its webhook receipt
intro: Use this after a sender has posted data. You can also inspect existing runs without sending anything new. The example is a real webhook run containing one fictional patient.
steps: In Runs, select the row matching the source and time you need.
Check Completed or Failed, then each node status. In this Bundle example, Form Validate is skipped because the FHIR branch handled the input.
Select a node row to inspect the data it received and produced. The example selects Persist store.
Select Output. Use Result or Logs for the other recorded details. A successful storage node does not prove a downstream recipient read the data.
Select Webhook receipts. Match the request identifier and status to the sender response. A queued or running receipt is not a completed run.
tasks.result: You can distinguish the accepted webhook request from the workflow execution and its node results.

tasks.title: Build a warehouse-count workflow
intro: Use this small read-only workflow to learn the canvas. It counts requests already in your warehouse. Zero is a valid result, so no sample data or database connector is needed.
steps: Return to the Workflows list and open the dots labelled Workflow actions.
Set Workflow name to a useful name. This example uses Warehouse row count.
In the Node library, search for Manual Trigger.
Drag Manual Trigger onto an empty part of the canvas.
Search for SQL Query and drag it beside the trigger. Clear the library search when finished.
Drag the dot on the right of Manual Trigger to the dot on the left of SQL Query. Confirm a line joins them.

tasks.title: Configure and run the warehouse count
intro: Continue with the two connected nodes. This read-only query counts requests already in your warehouse. Your count can differ from the example.
steps: Select SQL Query, then its Configure gear. In SQL (SELECT only), enter SELECT COUNT(*) AS requests FROM lab_requests. This query reads the reporting schema.
Select Run. The manual trigger waits for your next action.
Select the play badge labelled Click to run on Manual Trigger.
After Completed appears, open SQL Query and select Output. Read the requests value. Your count can differ from the picture.
tasks.result: The run completes in two steps and outputs one item containing the current request count.

tasks.title: Export a workflow definition
intro: Use this to keep a portable copy of a definition. Exported definitions can contain configuration, so review them before sharing.
steps: Return to the list and open the dots on the workflow row.
Select Export. The browser downloads a .workflow.json file. The list actions menu offers Import for this file format.
tasks.result: You have a JSON copy of the definition. Export does not run the workflow.

tasks.title: Make a separate copy
intro: Use Duplicate before experimenting with a saved custom workflow. The copy has its own definition.
steps: Open the dots beside the workflow you want to copy.
Select Duplicate. A new row ends with (copy). Open it before making changes.
tasks.result: The original and the copy appear separately.

tasks.title: Remove a custom workflow
intro: Use this only when you no longer need the definition. Delete permanently removes the selected custom workflow. The example removes the disposable copy.
steps: Open the custom workflow row dots and select Delete.
Read the name in the confirmation. Select Delete only for the definition you intend to remove.
tasks.result: The copy disappears and the original remains.

tasks.title: Import an exported definition
intro: Use this to add a workflow from an exported JSON file. Check the configuration before running an imported definition.
steps: Open the dots above the workflow list.
Select Import, then choose the exported .workflow.json file in your file picker.
tasks.result: The imported custom workflow appears in the list. Import does not run it.

tasks.title: Find workflows on a phone
intro: Use the workflow list on a phone. Build and configure canvas workflows on a larger screen.
steps: Use Search workflows to find the saved definition.
Select its name. Use History when you need its runs. A larger screen is better for canvas editing.

end.title: Send your own webhook payload
paragraphs: Use the URL shown in the webhook settings. Use HTTPS outside a local test installation. Send the saved secret only in X-Webhook-Token. Use an input your workflow accepts, such as a FHIR Bundle for Ingest.
From your installation folder, put your approved payload in data/your-payload.json. Replace the host and secret below. Read Start here for installed and development command locations.
html: A completed response contains ok, runId and correlationId. A 202 response means accepted, with a request identifier and polling URL. Follow that URL with the current token. Respect Retry-After. Reuse the same idempotency key and identical input for a retry. Different input with the same key returns 409.

end.title: Optional fictional practice files
paragraphs: Use these only in a test installation. Download one fictional patient Bundle to practise the webhook. Store it as data/your-payload.json in your installation folder, for example ~/Downloads/openldr_ce or C:\openldr_ce. Use the command above with your test host and token.
Download the two-node warehouse count workflow. Import it through Workflow actions if you want a reference after building your own. Neither file is required for normal use.

end.title: Choose other nodes
paragraphs: The Node library groups triggers, databases, communication, files and transformations. Search by the node name. A grey Coming soon entry cannot run.

Use Postgres, MySQL or Microsoft SQL with a matching enabled connector. SQL Query reads the reporting schema directly. Load Dataset reads saved workflow rows; Materialize Dataset replaces the rows saved under a dataset name.
Use Edit Fields, Filter, Switch, Pivot or Merge to transform items. Most text settings can read the incoming item with {{ $json.fieldName }}. Match the field names to the actual input you inspected.
File and delivery steps need their own setup. Scheduled reports covers datasets and Excel templates. Configure an approved email connector before adding delivery.

end.title: Handle interrupted webhook requests
paragraphs: History shows receipts separately from runs. Queued work can resume after a restart. Disabling, deleting or changing a workflow can cancel queued work. Interrupted means the result is unknown.

OpenLDR does not replay started work automatically. Check that the first worker stopped and reconcile outside effects before using a new request key. A failed connection does not prove nothing ran. Receipts remain after workflow deletion.
Headless operators can use the CLI receipt commands below. Read Start here for the installed launcher. In a development checkout, prefix these arguments with pnpm openldr.
html:
openldr workflows receipts list WORKFLOW_ID --limit 25 --offset 0 --json
openldr workflows receipts show REQUEST_ID --json

end.title: Restore a shipped workflow
paragraphs: System workflows offer Reset to default instead of Delete. Reset discards the customised graph and requires confirmation. Export the current definition first if you need to keep it.
Reset normally keeps the existing webhook secret. If the reset warning says it could not keep one, set a new secret and update every sender. This guide did not reset an operational workflow.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: Run waits without starting. Select the play badge on the trigger after Run.
A secret is rejected. Check the saved value and current path. Replacing a secret requires Save and, for Ingest, Save anyway. A saved secret cannot be revealed.
A node fails. Inspect its input, configuration and logs in History. Check required connector settings and the field names entering it.
Form capture says the pipeline is unavailable. Check that the shipped Ingest workflow is enabled. Do not clear or delete its nodes to troubleshoot a sender.
A delivery reports success. Check the recipient system separately. Node completion does not prove a person received or read the result.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Activity follows the payload lifecycle. Scheduled reports builds stored data and workbook output. Connectors configures external systems.
